import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The γ–θ conjecture

Does there exist a graph $G$ such that the domination number $\gamma(G)$, the eternal domination
number $\gamma_\infty(G)$ and the clique covering number $\theta(G)$ satisfy
$\gamma(G) = \gamma_\infty(G) < \theta(G)$?

Since $\gamma(G) \leq \gamma_\infty(G) \leq \theta(G)$ for every graph $G$, such a graph is
exactly a counterexample to the *γ–θ conjecture*, which states that
$\gamma(G) = \gamma_\infty(G)$ if and only if $\gamma(G) = \theta(G)$.

Here $\gamma_\infty$ is the eternal domination number in the *one-guard-moves* model of
Burger et al. (not the m-eternal domination number $\gamma_{\mathrm{m}}^\infty$ in which all
guards may move).

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Eternal dominating set, Open questions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eternal_dominating_set%23Open_questions)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [KM15a] W. F. Klostermeyer and C. M. Mynhardt, *Domination, Eternal Domination, and Clique
  Covering*, Discussiones Mathematicae Graph Theory 35 (2015), 283–300, Question 1.
  [arXiv:1407.5235](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5235)
- [KM15b] W. F. Klostermeyer and C. M. Mynhardt, *Protecting a graph with mobile guards*,
  Applicable Analysis and Discrete Mathematics 10 (2016), 1–29, Problem 33.
  [arXiv:1407.5228](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5228)
-/

namespace Conjecture

open SimpleGraph

variable {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)

/-
### Eternal domination (one-guard-moves model)

A configuration of guards is a finite set `D` of occupied vertices (at most one guard per
vertex). An attack occurs at a vertex `r`. If `r` is occupied nothing happens. Otherwise the
defender must move one guard from a vertex `v ∈ D` adjacent to `r` onto `r`, producing the
configuration `insert r (D.erase v)`. The defender must be able to answer every infinite
sequence of attacks in this way, and every configuration that arises must be a dominating set.

This is a safety game, so the defender wins from `D` if and only if `D` belongs to a family of
configurations that is closed under defending every possible attack. Such a family is called
*eternally secure* below.
-/

/-- A family `𝓕` of guard configurations is *eternally secure* for `G` if every configuration
in `𝓕` is a dominating set of `G`, and for every configuration `D ∈ 𝓕` and every unoccupied
vertex `r ∉ D`, some guard on a vertex `v ∈ D` adjacent to `r` can move to `r` so that the
resulting configuration `insert r (D.erase v)` again lies in `𝓕`. -/
def IsEternallySecure (𝓕 : Set (Finset V)) : Prop :=
  ∀ D ∈ 𝓕, G.IsDominating (D : Set V) ∧
    ∀ r ∉ D, ∃ v ∈ D, G.Adj v r ∧ insert r (D.erase v) ∈ 𝓕

/-- A finite set of vertices `D` is an *eternal dominating set* of `G` (in the one-guard-moves
model) if the defender, starting with one guard on each vertex of `D`, can defend every infinite
sequence of attacks by moving a single guard from a neighbour onto each attacked unoccupied
vertex, while always keeping the guards on a dominating set. Equivalently, `D` belongs to some
eternally secure family of configurations. -/
def IsEternalDominating (D : Finset V) : Prop :=
  ∃ 𝓕 : Set (Finset V), IsEternallySecure G 𝓕 ∧ D ∈ 𝓕

/-- The *eternal domination number* $\gamma_\infty(G)$ of `G` is the minimum size of an eternal
dominating set of `G` (one-guard-moves model). -/
noncomputable def eternalDominationNumber : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ D : Finset V, IsEternalDominating G D ∧ D.card = n}

/-- An eternal dominating set is a dominating set. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsEternalDominating.isDominating {D : Finset V} (h : IsEternalDominating G D) :
    G.IsDominating (D : Set V) := by
  obtain ⟨𝓕, h𝓕, hD⟩ := h
  exact (h𝓕 D hD).1

variable [Fintype V]

/-- The set of all vertices is an eternal dominating set: no vertex is ever unoccupied. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isEternalDominating_univ : IsEternalDominating G (Finset.univ : Finset V) :=
  ⟨{Finset.univ}, fun D hD => by
    simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hD
    subst hD
    exact ⟨fun v => Or.inl (by simp), fun r hr => (hr (Finset.mem_univ r)).elim⟩, rfl⟩

/-- The eternal domination number is at most the number of vertices. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem eternalDominationNumber_le_card : eternalDominationNumber G ≤ Fintype.card V :=
  Nat.sInf_le ⟨Finset.univ, isEternalDominating_univ G, Finset.card_univ⟩

/-- The domination number is at most the eternal domination number:
$\gamma(G) \leq \gamma_\infty(G)$. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem dominationNumber_le_eternalDominationNumber :
    G.dominationNumber ≤ eternalDominationNumber G := by
  refine csInf_le_csInf (OrderBot.bddBelow _)
    ⟨Fintype.card V, Finset.univ, isEternalDominating_univ G, Finset.card_univ⟩ ?_
  rintro n ⟨D, hD, rfl⟩
  exact ⟨D, hD.isDominating, rfl⟩

/-- In the path `0 - 1 - 2`, the dominating set `{1}` is not an eternal dominating set: after an
attack at `0` the guard must move to `0`, leaving `2` undominated. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isEternalDominating_pathGraph_three : ¬ IsEternalDominating (pathGraph 3) {1} := by
  rintro ⟨𝓕, h𝓕, h1⟩
  obtain ⟨v, hv, -, hmem⟩ := (h𝓕 {1} h1).2 0 (by decide)
  simp only [Finset.mem_singleton] at hv
  subst hv
  rw [show insert (0 : Fin 3) (({1} : Finset (Fin 3)).erase 1) = {0} by decide] at hmem
  have hdom := (h𝓕 {0} hmem).1 2
  simp [pathGraph_adj] at hdom

/-- The eternal domination number of the graph with no vertices is `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem eternalDominationNumber_of_isEmpty [IsEmpty V] : eternalDominationNumber G = 0 :=
  Nat.le_zero.mp <| (eternalDominationNumber_le_card G).trans_eq (Fintype.card_eq_zero)

/--
**The γ–θ conjecture** (open question).

Does there exist a (finite simple) graph $G$ such that the domination number $\gamma(G)$, the
eternal domination number $\gamma_\infty(G)$ (one-guard-moves model) and the clique covering
number $\theta(G)$ satisfy
$$\gamma(G) = \gamma_\infty(G) < \theta(G)?$$

Here the clique covering number $\theta(G)$, the minimum number of cliques partitioning the
vertices of $G$, is expressed as the chromatic number of the complement graph, $\chi(\overline G)$.

Since $\gamma(G) \leq \gamma_\infty(G) \leq \theta(G)$ always holds, such a graph exists if and
only if the γ–θ conjecture ("$\gamma(G) = \gamma_\infty(G)$ if and only if
$\gamma(G) = \theta(G)$ for every graph $G$") is false. Klostermeyer and Mynhardt [KM15a] proved
that any such graph must contain a triangle and have maximum degree at least four.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
      G.dominationNumber = eternalDominationNumber G ∧
        (G.dominationNumber : ℕ∞) < Gᶜ.chromaticNumber := by
  sorry

end Conjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot table is correct: the list entry is a yes/no existence question (Klostermeyer–Mynhardt Question 1 / Problem 33 of the survey), equivalent to the negation of the article's γ–θ conjecture via γ ≤ γ∞ ≤ θ. The 'must contain a triangle / Δ ≥ 4' facts are theorems and were only mentioned in the docstring, not formalized.
modeling_decisions: Finite simple graphs are quantified as `∃ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))`. Every finite graph is isomorphic to one on `Fin n` and all three invariants are isomorphism invariants; this also supplies `Fintype`/`DecidableEq` instances without existential instance arguments.

Eternal domination number is the one-guard-moves model (Burger et al.; Question 1 of Klostermeyer–Mynhardt arXiv:1407.5235), not the m-eternal (all-guards-move) number, as required by the decomposition notes and the Wikipedia article's chain γ ≤ γ∞ ≤ θ.

The defender's win of the infinite game is encoded as membership in an 'eternally secure' family (closed under defending every attack). This is the standard greatest-fixed-point characterisation of winning a safety game and is equivalent to the existence of a (possibly history-dependent) defender strategy that survives every infinite attack sequence.

Guard configurations are `Finset V` (at most one guard per vertex). Attacks on occupied vertices require no response (configuration unchanged), matching the article ('provided the attacked vertex has no guard on it') and the paper's 'assume w.l.o.g. r_i ∉ D_i'. Allowing optional moves on such attacks would not change the winning region since the attacker chooses the attacks.
The requirement that every configuration is a dominating set is included explicitly in `IsEternallySecure` (as in the paper's definition), although it is implied by the response condition.

Clique covering number θ(G) is expressed as `Gᶜ.chromaticNumber : ℕ∞` (chromatic number of the complement); a proper k-colouring of Ḡ is exactly a partition of V into ≤ k cliques of G. The comparison `γ < θ` casts the ℕ-valued domination number into ℕ∞. For finite graphs `Gᶜ.chromaticNumber` is finite.

Boundary: for n = 0 all three invariants are 0 and `0 < 0` is false, so the empty graph is not a spurious witness. `answer(True)` corresponds to the existence of such a graph (the γ–θ conjecture being false).

namespace Conjecture

/--
A set `D` of guard positions eternally dominates `G` in the one-guard-moves model if
there is a response to every finite history of attacks such that every resulting guard
configuration dominates `G`. An attack at an unoccupied vertex is answered by moving
exactly one guard there from an adjacent vertex. An attack at an occupied vertex leaves
the configuration unchanged.
-/
def IsEternalDominating {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (D : Finset V) : Prop :=
  ∃ response : List V → Finset V,
    response [] = D ∧
      ∀ attacks : List V,
        G.IsDominating (response attacks) ∧
          ∀ v : V,
            if v ∈ response attacks then
              response (attacks ++ [v]) = response attacks
            else
              ∃ u ∈ response attacks, G.Adj u v ∧
                response (attacks ++ [v]) = insert v ((response attacks).erase u)

/--
The eternal domination number `γ∞(G)` is the minimum number of guards in a
one-guard-moves eternal dominating set.
-/
noncomputable def eternalDominationNumber {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ D : Finset V, IsEternalDominating G D ∧ D.card = n}

/--
Does there exist a finite simple graph $G$ whose domination number, one-guard-moves
eternal domination number, and clique covering number satisfy
$\gamma(G)=\gamma_\infty(G)<\theta(G)$? Here $\theta(G)$ is represented as the
chromatic number of the complement of $G$.
-/

    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
      G.dominationNumber = eternalDominationNumber G ∧
        eternalDominationNumber G < Gᶜ.chromaticNumber.toNat := by
  sorry

end Conjecture
modeling_decisions: Finite simple graphs are represented as `SimpleGraph (Fin n)` for existentially quantified `n : ℕ`; this ranges, up to relabeling, over all finite simple graphs.
The yes/no wording is represented by `answer(sorry) ↔` the positive existence proposition.

The eternal domination number is the one-guard-moves parameter. A defender strategy maps each finite attack history to a guard-position finset, every such configuration must dominate the graph, and an attack at an unoccupied vertex moves exactly one guard from an adjacent vertex to the attacked vertex.

Attacks at already occupied vertices leave the configuration unchanged. The primary source assumes attacks are unoccupied without loss of generality, so this is the natural strategy extension to arbitrary attack histories and does not change the parameter.

The clique covering number `θ(G)` is represented by `Gᶜ.chromaticNumber.toNat`, using the primary source's equality `θ(G) = χ(complement G)`. The vertex type is finite, so the chromatic number is finite.

The minimum defining the eternal domination number uses `sInf` over natural cardinalities, matching the existing `SimpleGraph.dominationNumber` convention. The candidate set is nonempty on every finite graph because placing guards on every vertex is an eternal dominating configuration.

/-!
# The γ–θ conjecture

The *eternal domination game* (one-guard-moves model) is played on a finite graph $G$ by a
defender and an attacker. The defender first places guards on a dominating set $D_1$ (at most one
guard per vertex). Then, at each turn, the attacker attacks a vertex $r_i$. If $r_i$ is unoccupied,
the defender must move exactly one guard from a vertex of $D_i$ adjacent to $r_i$ onto $r_i$; the
new configuration $D_{i+1}$ must again be a dominating set. The defender wins if they can defend
every infinite sequence of attacks. A set $D$ is an *eternal dominating set* if the defender wins
when starting from $D$, and the *eternal domination number* $\gamma^\infty(G)$ is the minimum size
of an eternal dominating set.

The *clique covering number* $\theta(G)$ is the minimum number of cliques partitioning the
vertices of $G$; equivalently, it is the chromatic number of the complement of $G$.

Since $\gamma(G) \le \gamma^\infty(G) \le \theta(G)$ for every graph $G$, the *γ–θ conjecture*
(for every graph $G$, $\gamma(G) = \gamma^\infty(G)$ if and only if $\gamma(G) = \theta(G)$) is
equivalent to the non-existence of a graph $G$ with
$\gamma(G) = \gamma^\infty(G) < \theta(G)$. Whether such a graph exists is the first open question
of [KM15, Section 7] and is listed among the open problems of the survey [KM16, Section 10].

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Eternal dominating set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eternal_dominating_set%23Open_questions)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [KM15] Klostermeyer, W. F. and Mynhardt, C. M., *Domination, Eternal Domination, and Clique
  Covering*. Discussiones Mathematicae Graph Theory 35 (2015), 283–300.
  [arXiv:1407.5235](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5235)
- [KM16] Klostermeyer, W. F. and Mynhardt, C. M., *Protecting a graph with mobile guards*.
  Applicable Analysis and Discrete Mathematics 10 (2016), 1–29.
  [arXiv:1407.5228](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5228)
-/

namespace Conjecture

open SimpleGraph

variable {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

/-- A family `𝓔` of guard configurations (finite sets of occupied vertices) is *eternally
dominating* for `G` if every configuration `D ∈ 𝓔` is a dominating set and every attack at an
unoccupied vertex `r ∉ D` can be defended by moving one guard from a vertex `v ∈ D` adjacent to
`r` onto `r`, with the resulting configuration `insert r (D.erase v)` again in `𝓔`.

Such a family is exactly a set of positions from which the defender can win the eternal
domination game (one-guard-moves model) forever: it is an invariant of a winning strategy. -/
def IsEternalDominatingFamily (G : SimpleGraph V) (𝓔 : Set (Finset V)) : Prop :=
  ∀ D ∈ 𝓔, G.IsDominating (D : Set V) ∧
    ∀ r ∉ D, ∃ v ∈ D, G.Adj v r ∧ insert r (D.erase v) ∈ 𝓔

/-- A finite set of vertices `D` is an *eternal dominating set* of `G` if the defender, starting
with one guard on each vertex of `D`, can defend every infinite sequence of attacks in the eternal
domination game (one-guard-moves model). Equivalently, `D` belongs to some eternally dominating
family of configurations. -/
def IsEternalDominating (G : SimpleGraph V) (D : Finset V) : Prop :=
  ∃ 𝓔 : Set (Finset V), IsEternalDominatingFamily G 𝓔 ∧ D ∈ 𝓔

/-- The *eternal domination number* $\gamma^\infty(G)$ of a finite graph `G` is the minimum size
of an eternal dominating set of `G` (one-guard-moves model). -/
noncomputable def eternalDominationNumber (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ D : Finset V, IsEternalDominating G D ∧ D.card = n}

/-- The *domination number* $\gamma(G)$: the minimum size of a dominating set. -/
scoped notation "γ(" G ")" => SimpleGraph.dominationNumber G

/-- The *eternal domination number* $\gamma^\infty(G)$. -/
scoped notation "γ∞(" G ")" => eternalDominationNumber G

/-- The *clique covering number* $\theta(G)$: the minimum number of cliques of `G` covering all
vertices, which is the chromatic number of the complement of `G`. -/
scoped notation "θ(" G ")" => SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber Gᶜ

/-- Placing a guard on every vertex gives an eternal dominating set. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isEternalDominating_univ (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsEternalDominating G Finset.univ :=
  ⟨{Finset.univ}, fun D hD => by
    simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hD
    subst hD
    exact ⟨fun v => Or.inl (by simp), fun r hr => (hr (Finset.mem_univ r)).elim⟩, rfl⟩

omit [Fintype V] in
/-- Every eternal dominating set is a dominating set. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsEternalDominating.isDominating {G : SimpleGraph V} {D : Finset V}
    (hD : IsEternalDominating G D) : G.IsDominating (D : Set V) :=
  let ⟨_, h𝓔, hD⟩ := hD
  (h𝓔 D hD).1

/-- The domination number is at most the eternal domination number. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem dominationNumber_le_eternalDominationNumber (G : SimpleGraph V) : γ(G) ≤ γ∞(G) := by
  obtain ⟨D, hD, hcard⟩ := Nat.sInf_mem (s := {n | ∃ D : Finset V, IsEternalDominating G D ∧
    D.card = n}) ⟨_, Finset.univ, isEternalDominating_univ G, rfl⟩
  exact Nat.sInf_le ⟨D, hD.isDominating, hcard⟩

/-- The eternal domination number of a nonempty complete graph is `1`. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem eternalDominationNumber_top [Nonempty V] : γ∞((⊤ : SimpleGraph V)) = 1 := by
  unfold eternalDominationNumber
  apply le_antisymm
  · refine Nat.sInf_le ⟨{Classical.arbitrary V},
      ⟨Set.range ({·}), fun D hD => ?_, Set.mem_range_self _⟩, Finset.card_singleton _⟩
    obtain ⟨v, rfl⟩ := hD
    refine ⟨fun w => ?_, fun r hr => ⟨v, by simp, by simpa [eq_comm] using hr, ?_⟩⟩
    · by_cases hw : w = v
      · exact Or.inl (by simp [hw])
      · exact Or.inr ⟨v, by simp, hw⟩
    · simp

    (D : Finset V) : Prop :=
  ∃ strategy : List V → Finset V,

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The γ–θ conjecture

The *eternal domination number* $\gamma^\infty(G)$ of a finite simple graph $G$ is the smallest
number of mobile guards that can protect $G$ against every infinite sequence of attacks at
vertices in the *one-guard-moves* model: the guards initially occupy a dominating set, and
after each attack at an unoccupied vertex exactly one guard moves from an adjacent vertex onto
the attacked vertex, in such a way that the guards always occupy a dominating set.

For every graph $G$ one has $\gamma(G) \le \gamma^\infty(G) \le \theta(G)$, where $\gamma(G)$
is the domination number and $\theta(G)$ is the clique covering number. The *γ–θ conjecture*
states that $\gamma(G) = \gamma^\infty(G)$ if and only if $\gamma(G) = \theta(G)$; a
counterexample would be exactly a graph $G$ with $\gamma(G) = \gamma^\infty(G) < \theta(G)$.
Whether such a graph exists is the first open question posed by Klostermeyer and Mynhardt
[KM15a, Section 7].

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Eternal dominating set: Open questions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eternal_dominating_set%23Open_questions)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [KM15a] Klostermeyer, W. F. and Mynhardt, C. M., *Domination, Eternal Domination, and Clique
  Covering*. Discuss. Math. Graph Theory 35 (2015), 283–300.
  [arXiv:1407.5235](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5235)
- [KM15b] Klostermeyer, W. F. and Mynhardt, C. M., *Protecting a graph with mobile guards*.
  Appl. Anal. Discrete Math. 10 (2016), 1–29. [arXiv:1407.5228](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5228)
-/

namespace Conjecture

open SimpleGraph

variable {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)

/-- A guard move of `G` in the one-guard-moves model: in response to an attack at the vertex `r`,
the configuration of guards `D` (a set of occupied vertices) is changed to `D'` by moving a
single guard from a vertex `v ∈ D` adjacent to `r` onto `r`. -/
def IsGuardMove (D D' : Finset V) (r : V) : Prop :=
  ∃ v ∈ D, G.Adj v r ∧ D' = insert r (D.erase v)

/-- A family `𝓕` of guard configurations is an *eternal family* of `G` if every configuration
in `𝓕` is a dominating set of `G`, and every attack at an unoccupied vertex of a configuration
in `𝓕` can be defended by a single guard move leading to a configuration in `𝓕`.

Since the eternal domination game is a safety game, the defender can protect the graph forever
starting from `D` (against every, possibly adaptive, attacker) if and only if `D` belongs to
some eternal family. -/
def IsEternalFamily (𝓕 : Set (Finset V)) : Prop :=
  ∀ D ∈ 𝓕, G.IsDominating (D : Set V) ∧ ∀ r ∉ D, ∃ D' ∈ 𝓕, IsGuardMove G D D' r

/-- A finite set of vertices `D` is an *eternal dominating set* of `G` (in the one-guard-moves
model) if guards initially placed on `D` can defend every infinite sequence of attacks: each
attack at an unoccupied vertex is answered by moving one guard from an adjacent vertex onto the
attacked vertex, and the guards occupy a dominating set at all times. -/
def IsEternalDominating (D : Finset V) : Prop :=
  ∃ 𝓕 : Set (Finset V), IsEternalFamily G 𝓕 ∧ D ∈ 𝓕

dominating set of `G` in the one-guard-moves model. -/

  sInf {n | ∃ D : Finset V, IsEternalDominating G D ∧ D.card = n}

/-- The set of all vertices of a finite graph is an eternal dominating set. -/

theorem isEternalDominating_univ [Fintype V] : IsEternalDominating G Finset.univ :=

    subst hD
    exact ⟨fun v => Or.inl (by simp), fun r hr => (hr (Finset.mem_univ r)).elim⟩, rfl⟩

  Nat.sInf_le ⟨Finset.univ, isEternalDominating_univ G, Finset.card_univ⟩

  rintro n ⟨D, ⟨𝓕, h𝓕, hD⟩, hn⟩
  exact ⟨D, (h𝓕 D hD).1, hn⟩

    · by_cases h : u = w

    · exact fun h => hr (by simp [h]), v, rfl⟩

  refine le_csInf ⟨1, {v}, isEternalDominating_top_singleton v, by simp⟩ ?_
  rintro n ⟨D, ⟨𝓕, h𝓕, hD⟩, rfl⟩
  rw [Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero, Ne, Finset.card_eq_zero]
  rintro rfl
  simpa using (h𝓕 _ hD).1 v
